---
title: "Software"
---

Open-source tools I've built for spatial transcriptomics, single-cell analysis, and AI-driven bioinformatics — on [my GitHub](https://github.com/jrose835) and the [Santangelo Lab's](https://github.com/santangelo-lab).

::: {.entry}
[CRISP](https://github.com/santangelo-lab/CRISP){.entry-title}
<div class="entry-meta">R & Python · segmentation quality assessment</div>
Assesses cell segmentation quality in spatial transcriptomics data by identifying cells that co-express mutually exclusive marker genes. Produces negative-coexpression segmentation purity metrics and supports Xenium, Seurat, and SpatialExperiment objects. Described in [our preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.04.16.718947v1).
:::

::: {.entry}
[Stringency](https://github.com/santangelo-lab/stringency){.entry-title}
<div class="entry-meta">Python · governance for LLM-driven pipelines</div>
Pre-execution admissibility checks, append-only provenance, and human-in-the-loop holds for LLM-driven bioinformatics pipelines — so agent-run analyses stay reproducible and auditable.
:::

::: {.entry}
[Xen_Segmentation_NextFlow](https://github.com/jrose835/Xen_Segmentation_NextFlow){.entry-title}
<div class="entry-meta">Nextflow pipeline · Python</div>
A custom Nextflow pipeline for generating alternative cell segmentations (nuclear expansion, Baysor, and others) for 10x Xenium in situ data.
:::

::: {.entry}
[Xen_Seurat_Pipeline](https://github.com/jrose835/Xen_Seurat_Pipeline){.entry-title}
<div class="entry-meta">R pipeline · Seurat</div>
Processes 10x Xenium spatial single-cell data with Seurat: QC, normalization, integration, clustering, and annotation in a reproducible workflow.
:::

::: {.entry}
[Xen_TMA_pipeline](https://github.com/jrose835/Xen_TMA_pipeline){.entry-title}
<div class="entry-meta">Python pipeline</div>
A processing pipeline for tissue microarrays run on the Xenium platform — splits multi-punch arrays into per-sample datasets for downstream analysis.
:::

::: {.entry}
[pyMFI](https://github.com/jrose835/pyMFI){.entry-title}
<div class="entry-meta">Python</div>
Calculates per-cell mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) from imaging data.
:::
